criteria.justification: The response opens with a clear, unambiguous decision: 'I would order an immediate rollback of the new launch,' with no hedging or listing of unresolved options.

The response implies the rollback is temporary and undoable ('rollout has been temporarily paused,' 'we will notify them when it is re-enabled,' 'customers will ultimately forgive a delayed integration'), suggesting reversibility of the chosen path, but it never explicitly frames this as a reversibility tradeoff versus the fast-fix alternative.

The response directly contrasts the two costs: 'rolling back a publicly announced feature is embarrassing' versus 'leaving core functionality broken for existing customers for several days is catastrophic,' and later states 'PR embarrassment is temporary; breaking your core product is a fundamental failure of reliability.'

The response explicitly rejects pushing a rushed fix, instead giving engineering 'the several days they need to build, thoroughly test, and QA the proper scoping fix without the pressure of a live, high-severity incident.'

Beyond the rollback, the response lays out a full follow-up plan: support scripts for both customer groups, a public status page update, engineering time to build the proper fix, and a leadership briefing including 'the estimated timeline for the re-launch.'
